summary: This RFC describes procedures for using multipoint BFD to detect data plane failures on point-to-multipoint MPLS label switched paths and Segment Routing point-to-multipoint policies using SR-MPLS. It also updates an earlier RFC related to these mechanisms.

eli5.summary: When one speaker talks to many listeners, you want to know if any listener lost the signal. This is a quick way for the network to notice.

questions: how to detect failures on p2mp mpls paths
how to detect p2mp lsp failures
what is the dummy ipv6 prefix 100:0:0:1::/64
what is an active tail in bfd
subtitle: How multipoint BFD watches point-to-multipoint MPLS paths for failures, and which IPv6 dummy address to use for it.

tldr.problem: RFC 8562 defines multipoint BFD, but running it over point-to-multipoint MPLS Label Switched Paths and Segment Routing P2MP policies needs concrete encapsulation, bootstrapping and failure-notification procedures. The old IPv4-mapped loopback destination address for IPv6 was also a poor fit.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines IP/UDP and non-IP (G-ACh) encapsulations, bootstraps tails with LSP Ping or the control plane, and specifies how an active tail tells the head about a failure. It recommends the new Dummy IPv6 Prefix 100:0:0:1::/64 as the destination.
tldr.outcome: Operators get a complete way to detect data plane failures on P2MP LSPs. The RFC updates RFC 8562 on the IPv6 destination address choice.

today: RFC 9780 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2025. It is not obsoleted and has no later updates listed. It updates RFC 8562 on the IPv6 destination address for MPLS echo requests.

sections.title: Multipoint BFD on MPLS Paths
sections.content:
RFC 8562 uses Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) to monitor failures between a sender, the head, and one or more receivers, the tails, in multipoint networks. It adds two session types, MultipointHead and MultipointTail.

This document applies those modes to point-to-multipoint (P2MP) MPLS Label Switched Paths (LSPs) and to Segment Routing (SR) P2MP policies with an SR-MPLS data plane. It also covers using LSP Ping or out-of-band methods to bootstrap a BFD session, and the behavior of an active tail that notifies the head.
sections.eli5: One teacher (the head) calls out to a whole class (the tails). This RFC explains how the teacher and class check that everyone can still hear.

sections.title: The Dummy IPv6 Prefix and IP Encapsulation
sections.content:
In multipoint BFD the head sends every BFD Control packet with Your Discriminator set to zero, so a tail cannot demultiplex sessions the usual way. A tail instead uses the source IP address, My Discriminator and the identity of the multipoint tree. With IP/UDP encapsulation the source IP address MUST be used.

Historically the destination had to be in the IPv6-mapped IPv4 loopback block ::ffff:127.0.0.1/128. That is not analogous to the IPv4 loopback, and using a loopback destination violates Section 2.5.3 of RFC 4291. IANA therefore allocated the Dummy IPv6 Prefix 100:0:0:1::/64. This RFC updates Section 5.8 of RFC 8562: the sender of an MPLS echo request SHOULD use an address from that block, and MAY still pick one from ::ffff:7f00/104. Using the old block is discouraged.

If several alternative paths exist for a P2MP LSP, the MultipointHead SHOULD use the Entropy Label used for LSP Ping to exercise them, or MAY use the UDP port number.
sections.eli5: The old way of addressing the messages was like writing "to myself" on a letter. The new way is a proper made-up address that exists just for these test messages.

sections.title: Non-IP Encapsulation
sections.content:
Extra IP/UDP headers add overhead, and validation of them can fail for reasons unrelated to the MPLS label stack or BFD. Avoiding them improves how accurately a detected failure points to a defect in the LSP. So the RFC defines a more compact encapsulation using the Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh).

The packet MUST use the G-ACh Label (GAL) at the bottom of the label stack, followed by an Associated Channel Header (ACH). The Channel Type MUST be 0x0013, Multipoint BFD Session. A Source Address TLV from RFC 7212 MUST immediately follow the BFD Control packet, so a tail can learn who the MultipointHead is and demultiplex correctly.
sections.eli5: It is a slimmer envelope. Fewer wrappers means fewer ways for the message to go wrong, and a failure is easier to blame on the right thing.

sections.title: Bootstrapping a Session
sections.content:
A tail must learn that a session exists. LSP Ping MAY be used. It MUST include the Target FEC Stack TLV and the BFD Discriminator TLV. For P2MP MPLS LSPs the Target FEC Stack TLV uses the sub-TLVs from Section 3.1 of RFC 6425, and for SR P2MP policies with SR-MPLS the procedures of RFC 8287 MUST be followed. Setting Reply Mode to "Do not reply" is RECOMMENDED, since a tail's echo reply has nothing useful to tell the head under Demand mode.

A MultipointTail receiving such an LSP Ping MUST validate it, associate the discriminator with the P2MP LSP, create a P2MP BFD session with bfd.SessionType = MultipointTail, and use the source IP address, the discriminator and the LSP identity to demultiplex sessions.

LSP Ping SHOULD also be used periodically to check that the control plane matches the data plane, at a rate significantly lower than the BFD Control packet rate. Alternatively, the BFD Discriminator attribute MAY be used from the control plane, following Section 3.1.6 of RFC 9026.
sections.eli5: Before the class can listen for the teacher, each student needs to be told which teacher to expect. A special ping carries that introduction.

sections.title: Active Tail and Head Notification
sections.content:
With plain RFC 8562 procedures an egress LSR can detect a failure, but the ingress LSR does not know the state of the P2MP LSP. RFC 8563 defines an active tail, and this document specifies the simplest method, Head Notification without Polling. On the ingress, bfd.SessionType is MultipointHead and bfd.RequiredMinRxInterval is nonzero. On the egress, it is MultipointTail and bfd.SilentTail is zero.

When an egress LSR detects a failure, it sends a BFD Control packet with the Poll bit set, Status Down, Diagnostic Control Detection Time Expired, and Your Discriminator set to the value it uses to demultiplex that session. The packet MAY use IP/UDP with the ingress LSR as destination and UDP port 4784, or PW-ACH encapsulation with Channel Type 0x0007.

Packets go out once per second until a valid packet with the Final bit arrives from the ingress, or the defect clears. The egress SHOULD initially send three in quick succession, and periodic transmission MUST be jittered, reducing the interval by a random 0 to 25%. The ingress answers with a unicast packet with the Final bit set. If many egress LSRs report at once, the ingress control plane could be congested, so an implementation is RECOMMENDED to rate-limit received BFD Control packets passed to the control plane.
sections.eli5: If a student stops hearing the teacher, they raise a hand once a second until the teacher nods back. They wait a slightly random time so the whole class does not shout at once.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The document introduces no new security considerations and inherits those of RFC 5880, RFC 5884, RFC 7726, RFC 8562, RFC 8029 and RFC 6425. BFD for P2MP MPLS LSPs MUST follow Section 4.1 of RFC 4687 to avoid congestion in the control or data plane from the rate of BFD Control packets.

Operators SHOULD weigh the extra traffic when picking the head's transmit interval. IP/UDP encapsulation adds up to 28 octets, more than 50% of the BFD Control packet length, compared to G-ACh encapsulation.
sections.eli5: Do not let the checking messages become so many that they clog the road. The slim envelope helps.

sections.title: IANA Allocations
sections.content:
IANA allocated 100:0:0:1::/64 as the "Dummy IPv6 Prefix" in the IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Registry, with allocation date 2025-04. It is a valid source only: Destination, Forwardable, Globally Reachable and Reserved-by-Protocol are all False.

IANA also allocated G-ACh Type 0x0013, "Multipoint BFD Session", referencing this RFC.
sections.eli5: The official registry now has a reserved address block and a reserved channel number for this job.
